edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Brief early-day naps can improve alertness and memory consolidation without stealing too much pressure from nighttime sleep.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2021 Dutheil meta analysis in Int J Environ Res Public Health, which suggests that short early-day naps tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for cognitive function. Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
